newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA REPLACE RONALDO WITH RIVALDO - TV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA REPLACE RONALDO WITH RIVALDO - TV.

text.p: Barcelona, at least $26 million richer from the sale of Ronaldo to Inter Milan, were reported on Thursday to have signed Deportivo Coruna's Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo for the same amount.
Earlier, sources close to English club Liverpool said Barcelona were chasing England midfielder Steve McManaman for a reported 12 million pounds ($19 million).
Spanish state television said in an unsourced report that league runners-up Barcelona would pay four billion pesetas ($25.8 million) to buy out Rivaldo's contract.
It gave no other details. Friday is the transfer deadline for clubs competing in the Champions' League.
Internazionale recently paid four billion pesetas to buy out Ronaldo's contract with Barcelona.
The 20-year-old Brazilian was under contract to Barcelona until 2004 but had a withdrawal clause in his contract allowing him to buy himself out.

That transfer is still being hammered out by FIFA, with Barcelona reportedly seeking a further 2.2 billion pesetas ($14.6 million) as a transfer fee. Inter are said to have offered only 100 million pesetas ($660,000).

Last month Barcelona signed Brazilian striker Sonny Anderson from Monaco for between $16 and $20 million and have also signed French international Christophe Dugarry and Dutchman Michael Reiziger from AC Milan.
A Deportivo official waved away reporters during a soccer match when asked to confirm the Rivaldo move.
Rivaldo joined Deportivo from Brazilian club Palmeiras in July 1996 and scored 21 goals last season.
There was no official word on either reported deal from any of the clubs involved.
Sources in Liverpool said McManaman was in Barcelona on Thursday for talks with the club.
Barcelona general manager Bobby Robson, now overseeing signings at the club, was at Anfield on Wednesday to watch McManaman in a premier league match against Leicester.
McManaman's contract expires at the end of next season, leaving Liverpool the option of cashing in or facing the prospect of losing him for no reward.
